title: Cap. 3 Obj. 15: Wisely destined means do not exceed their adequate end — the elect’s salvation
pass_a_gloss: Obj.15: wisely destined means ≤ adequate end; adequate end = elect’s salvation → no ordination to non-elect → not applicable-to-all. Sol: grant elect’s infallible salvation is special/eximious end under God’s glory; deny sole/unique end. Also so remission+eternal life can be generally offered/conferred if they believe — presupposes applicable-to-all + applied on believing. Jn 3:14-15; 6:40; Acts 10:43. Non-elect make ordination useless by unbelief, don’t nullify it (else unbeliever could plead even-if-I-believed). Prosper cup: in itself profits all; if not drunk, doesn’t heal — capacity from general ordination; non-drinking from common unbelief; drinking from special mercy.
pass_b_english: Obj. 15. Means wisely destined do not exceed their adequate end: But the adequate end of Christ’s death is the salvation of the elect: Therefore Christ’s death has no ordination to any other non-elect whatever: Therefore it is falsely established as applicable to all human beings by God’s ordination.

Sol. I acknowledge that the infallible salvation of the elect is, under the glory of God, a certain special and outstanding end for attaining which Christ’s death was destined: Yet I deny that it was the unique or sole end. For God sent his Son into the world, and willed him to die, not only that he might efficaciously save the elect, but also that remission of sins and eternal life might be generally offered to any human beings whatever in the Gospel, and even conferred, if they believed. But this general or conditional covenant is not understood as established unless Christ’s death by God’s ordination is presupposed applicable to all human beings, and to be applied in fact to anyone as soon as he has believed. Scripture has clearly indicated this end in many places: ([[John 3:14–15 >> Bible:John 3:14]]): As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that everyone who believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. And ([[John 6:40 >> Bible:John 6:40]]): This is the will of my Father who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life. ([[Acts 10:43 >> Bible:Acts 10:43]]): To him all the Prophets bear witness, that through his name everyone who believes in him receives remission of sins. I pass over the rest. From these it is plain enough that, although not all but the elect alone believe, God specially softening their hearts, yet Christ’s death was so offered by the Son to God the Father, so also offered indiscriminately by God the Father to human beings, so announced promiscuously to all by Evangelical ministers, that anyone may gather from this that there is a certain firm and stable ordination of God according to which Christ’s death pertains to all human beings. The non-elect by their unbelief make this ordination useless to themselves: but they do not make such an ordination to be counted as nothing, or to be acknowledged as by no means established by Christ’s death as regards these unbelievers. For if we admit this, any unbeliever could plead, Even if I had believed the Gospel, I would not have been freed from sins by Christ’s death, because Christ’s death had no ordination according to which I could have been partaker of it. Which is diametrically contrary to the words of Christ himself ([[John 3:17–18 >> Bible:John 3:17]]): God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world might be saved through him. Whoever believes in him is not condemned; but whoever does not believe is already condemned, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God. And this is what holy Prosper says: The death of Christ has indeed in itself what would profit all; but if it is not drunk, it does not heal. That it has in itself what can profit all, it has from the general Divine ordination: but that it is not drunk by many through faith, happens from common human unbelief: that it is drunk by some, comes from special Divine pity.
